source.label: thm:ecpupperbound
source.quote:
Let \( f \in \text{Lip}(k) \) be a non-constant function over a compact domain \( \mathcal{X} \subset \mathbb{R}^d \), and let ECPv2 be tuned with any \( \delta \in [0,1) \), integer \( m \geq 1 \), $\beta>1$, \( \varepsilon_1 > 0 \), \( \tau_{n,d} > 1 \), and \( C > 1 \). Then for any budget \( n \in \mathbb{N}^\star \) and confidence level \( \xi \in (0, 1 - \frac{1}{\beta^2}) \), with probability at least \( 1 - \frac{1}{\beta^2} - \xi \), the simple regret satisfies:
\[
\mathcal{R}_{\text{ECPv2}, f}(n)
\leq
k \cdot
\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{X}) \cdot \log_{\tau_{n,d}}\left(\frac{k}{\varepsilon_1}\right)^{\frac{1}{d}}
\left(  \frac{\ln(1/\xi)}{ n } \right)^{\frac{1}{d}}.
\]

results.notes: The paper's n is the horizon T, its k is L_lip and its rad/diam map to r_K/diam_K. The precedence of log_tau(k/eps_1)^(1/d) is taken literally as (log_tau(k/eps_1))^(1/d). The expression uses tau as a fixed symbol, but the paper's default tau_{n,d} depends on n. The noise-free deterministic function is recorded with environment stochastic_iid because no deterministic option exists. Theorem 1 (asymptotic no-regret, with regret converging to 0 in probability) is not recorded separately because it gives no rate. The proof has gaps, e.g. it uses i_star^(1/d) as a bound on (n/(n-i*+1))^(1/d).
